reference: Independent closed-form complex-impedance implementation of selected IEC 60909-0:2016 kernels, the EasyPower/Parise legacy CCM equation set, and three Schneider Electric published cross-checks, written from the standard and the published documents by bench-src/gen_protectioncoordination.py; no Protection Coordination Studio code is imported and the generator never reads the artifact or the page.
reference_citations: IEC 60909-0:2016, 4.3.1.2 eq. (55)-(56) and method C - i_p = kappa sqrt(2) I_k'', kappa = 1.02 + 0.98 exp(-3 R/X), R/X = (R_c/X_c)(f_c/f) at f_c = 0.4 f
IEC 60909-0:2016, 6.1 eq. (5)-(6) - network feeder impedance and its referral
IEC 60909-0:2016, 6.2 eq. (7)-(9) - two-winding transformer Z_T, R_T, X_T
IEC 60909-0:2016, 6.6 eq. (18) - Z_G = x_d'' U_rG^2/S_rG; the K_G correction is NOT applied, see reference_limits
EasyPower 11.1 Help, TCC Options, Characteristic Current Method - i_dc(0.5 cycle) and equivalent X/R equations; cites G. Parise, IEEE Trans. Industry Applications 31(1), 1995
Schneider Electric 0100DB2301 Electrical Distribution Fundamentals Design Guide, System Protection - delta-wye secondary L-N fault gives 57.7% of maximum three-phase primary fault current
Schneider Electric 0100DB2301, System Protection, Add a Generator / Figure 55 - bus 02 19.318 kA before and 24.672 kA after adding the 15 MW generator (926.2 A rated, x_d'' = 19%)
Schneider Electric FA405803 - 400 kVA / 410 V / u_kr 4% transformer, I_k'' = I_rT/u_kr on a stiff primary
reference_limits: IEC 60909-0:2016 6.1 eq. (6) writes Z_Q = c U_nQ^2/S_kQ″, so eq. (29) at the feeder terminals returns the quoted I_kQ″. The tool uses Z_Q = U_nQ^2/S_kQ″ and applies c only in the equivalent voltage source, which makes its terminal current c x the quoted value: 13 777.68 A against 13 121.60 A for the 250 MVA / 11 kV feeder of analytic_source_3ph. The tool's own regression test asserts the factor c, so this is a declared convention and not a slip. The cases here take Z_Q = U_nQ^2/S_kQ″ as a stated case input and grade only eq. (29)/(31)/(34)/(52)/(55)/(56) on it; the mapping (U_n, S_kQ″) -> Z_Q is NOT established by this benchmark. The four cases that run at c = 1 are unaffected, because there the two conventions coincide.

The generator impedance correction K_G of IEC 60909-0:2016 6.6 eq. (18) is not applied by the tool and cannot be computed from its generator inputs, which carry no rated power factor. The generator branch reference is Z_G = x_d″ U^2/S_rG as entered, so K_G is NOT established.

The six networks are the fixtures of the tool's own regression tests. A fixture is an input, not a reference: every reference value above is computed in this file from the cited clause, and none of them is read back from the tool.
tolerance: The tolerances of the 2026-08-12 artifact are kept unchanged so that a verdict can be compared with it: current KPIs +-0.005 kA, kappa +-0.0005, CCM X/R +-0.005, the L-L/3-phase ratio +-0.0008 absolute, the 57.7% transformer ratio +-0.002 absolute, and the Schneider generator increment 0.5% relative because the published diagram values and generator data are rounded. No tolerance was widened; the observed deviation is recorded next to every graded value.

cases.note: For Z2=Z1, IEC line-line current is sqrt(3)/2 of three-phase current.
Finite utility source impedance referred through 11 kV/410 V ratio and added to 4% transformer impedance.
Independent phasor sum of two source currents at a common 11 kV bus; CCM is evaluated from the two branch magnitudes/XR values.

Ik_kA.clause: IEC 60909-0:2016 4.2 eq. (29) on the parallel equivalent

utility_kA.clause: IEC 60909-0:2016 4.2 eq. (29) on the feeder branch alone

generator_kA.clause: IEC 60909-0:2016 4.2 eq. (29) on the generator branch alone

ccm_xr.clause: EasyPower 11.1 / Parise CCM over the two branches

kappa.clause: IEC 60909-0:2016 4.3.1.2 eq. (56), method C on the 0.4f parallel equivalent

cases.note: Schneider 0100DB2301 states a secondary L-N fault on a delta-wye transformer produces 57.7% of the maximum three-phase primary phase current.

primary_phase_ratio.clause: Schneider Electric 0100DB2301, System Protection: secondary L-N fault gives 57.7% of the maximum three-phase primary phase current
primary_phase_ratio.ref_exact_note: (1/sqrt3) x 3|Z_1| / |2 Z_1 + Z_0| for the finite feeder of this case; the published 57.7% is its Z_Q -> 0 limit

notes: primary_phase_ratio: Diagram.record.build() carries no per-device current, so the graded channel is deviceCurrentForFault(QHV577, fault).phase; the dom channel is the trip timeline, which prints integer amps.

cases.note: Schneider 0100DB2301 Add a Generator / Figure 55 publishes 19.318 kA before and 24.672 kA after the 15 MW generator; the branch increment is therefore 5.354 kA. Only the generator increment is graded; the total remains an explicit convention cross-check.

generator_kA.clause: Schneider Electric 0100DB2301 Figure 55 published branch increment 24.672-19.318 kA
generator_kA.ref_closed_form_note: c I_rG / x_d″ from IEC 6.6 Z_G (no K_G); equals 1.1 x 926.2 / 0.19 A

notes: generator_kA: the record CCM inversion is singular here (both branches are entered with the same X/R), so this quantity is graded on the page function and not on the record surface

channels.record: Diagram.record.build().outputs, the published calculation-record surface, double precision.
channels.dom: the printed strings of #kFault / #kIp / #kCCM / #ccmTable / #timeline, read with a separator-tolerant parser. This is the channel the 2026-08-12 artifact graded on.
channels.page_fn: a read through one of the page's own pure functions (calc.fault.sources, deviceCurrentForFault), used where the record surface carries no counterpart.

environment: Chromium (Playwright) on Linux, http://127.0.0.1:8332 origin, ?lang=en. Every case state is driven in through the page's own project-import control (#fileImport) and nothing is written into page state. References generated by python3 bench-src/gen_protectioncoordination.py.
crosscheck: Three published cross-checks are carried un-graded beside the graded closed forms, because each needs a convention the published source does not expose: Schneider FA405803 I_rT/u_kr for transformer_referral (0.099 % from the closed form that includes the finite feeder), and Schneider 0100DB2301 Figure 55 bus 02 before and after for schneider_generator_increment (1.70 % and 1.29 % from the closed form). The graded Figure-55 quantity is the branch increment alone.
not_benchmarked: Generic circuit-breaker, fuse and relay TCC shapes, the automatic grading optimizer and the protection-zone visualization: they are engineering models/UI workflows rather than a single standard reference curve.

User-imported manufacturer TCC and selectivity/back-up datasets: parsing/applicability logic has self-tests, but correctness of proprietary manufacturer tables depends on the user-provided source and is not independently benchmarked here.
CT ALF/knee-voltage/saturation screening beyond its algebraic self-tests.

The IEC 60909-0:2016 mu/q breaking-current screening over arbitrary multi-source networks, the conservative idc source-branch envelope, and the full IEC 60909 d.c. component equation (64). The latter is not yet implemented.

Steady-state synchronous-generator IEC equations (84)/(85): the tool currently uses explicit user/vendor IkP data as a screen; converter/UPS stationary and unbalanced-fault control behavior remains vendor-specific.
IEC m+n thermal-equivalent/Joule-integral calculation: the current cable check is a branch-current I^2 t / user Ithr,1s screening only.
IT first-fault capacitive current, arc-flash, differential/distance/directional protection and proprietary manufacturer back-up/selectivity tables not supplied by the user.
Equation-level changes between IEC 60909-0:2016 and IEC 60909-0:2026 have not been independently reconciled; 2016 equation-set features are labelled explicitly in the tool.
The network feeder impedance convention of IEC 60909-0:2016 6.1 eq. (6) and the generator correction K_G of 6.6 eq. (18): see reference_limits.
The TCC canvas, including the --tcc-ink/--tcc-grid tokens this page gained on 2026-10-15; no pixel is graded here.
provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/gen_protectioncoordination.py from the clauses and published documents this artifact cites. That generator reads no page, no artifact and nothing it writes, so no case reuses a stored value and none carries ref_source "recorded". The six networks are the fixtures of the page's own regression tests; a fixture is an input, not a reference.
